newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India shares rise in contrast to Bombay.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India shares rise in contrast to Bombay.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts closed higher, despite falls in local markets, as a strong earnings report in the automotive sector spurred investor demand, traders said.
After trading in India closed, Truckmaker TELCO gave the GDR market a boost, reporting earnings of 7.62 billion rupees, well above expectations, traders said.
The Bombay 30 share index lost 9.10 points to 3,692.55.
But the fall in Bombay had little effect in London.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.64 points up at 82.16, with the premium over the local market at 27.63 percent from 25.63 percent.
"Despite the fact that GDRs are sentiment driven, they are in short supply," a trader said.
Traders say they expect the local market to catch up after a strong recent run by GDRs, but do not expect a narrowing of the GDR premium.
TELCO finished up 34 cents at $12.75/$13.75 and Bajaj Auto gained 25 cents to $32.00/$33.50.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 0.17 points, or 0.17 percent, to 114.65, representing a discount to the local market of 3.12 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index lost 0.35 points to 67.75 points, a premium of 41.33 percent over the local market.
